newsitem.title: USA: Anti-government activists guilty in Florida trial.
newsitem.headline: Anti-government activists guilty in Florida trial.

text.p: Seven members of the Constitutional Common Law Court anti-government group were found guilty by a federal jury on Wednesday of threatening U.S. and state judges and jurors.
Those convicted included Emilio Ippolito, 71, the founder of the Tampa-based group, and his daughter, Susan Mokdad, 41. An eighth defendant, Toby Brown, was found not guilty.
U.S. prosecutors said members of the group interfered with trials in Florida and California and sent letters threatening to arrest or kidnap judges and jurors.
Each of the convicted could get up to 200 years in prison at sentencing, according to U.S. Attorney Charles Wilson. "We are obviously very pleased with the verdicts," he said.
Several judges testified during the 10-week trial that they feared for their safety after they received written warnings from the group members.
But the defendants said they never harmed or intended to harm anyone, that their actions were an expression of free speech and political dissent.
"All we wanted to do was make judges accountable. We had no intention to harm anybody," Ippolito testified.

Ippolito was removed from the courtroom at the start of the trial after he called presiding U.S. Judge Steven Merryday a traitor. He was allowed to return six weeks later to testify on his own behalf.

The trial was held under tight security. U.S. Marshals were inside and outside the courtroom at U.S. District Court in Tampa and anyone who attended the trial had to pass through two metal detectors and show a photo identification card.
